digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center reconciliation harness and live mutation test suite
propositions: A reconciliation pass against a real Jira Data Center instance with a complete scrubbed copy of the production ticket store must demonstrate bidirectional data movement: issues created in DC must appear in the local store after inbound reconciliation, and local ticket edits must appear on DC issues after outbound reconciliation.

The harness test environment must be physically isolated from production: the working repo must have no git remotes, REBAR_SYNC_PUSH must be off, and no Cloud credentials must be present in the job environment, asserted by tests rather than assumed.

The store copy must be obtained by explicitly fetching the orphan tickets branch and extracting it into .tickets-tracker/, with completeness verified by counting local ticket entries and comparing against the branch content, to catch partial extractions.

All reconciler artifacts and production Jira bindings must be scrubbed from the store copy by matching and removing all .bridge_state* directories and their contents, verified by a test assertion that no such artifacts survive anywhere in the copied tree.

Each of the 28 mutation cells (14 inbound × 14 outbound, plus converged-pair idempotence and pagination cases) must assert a specific oracle proving the mutation round-tripped: the mutation must be applied on one side, a reconciliation pass run, and the changed value read back from the other side to verify it arrived.

Three product limitations on Data Center (sub-task parent cannot be moved or cleared, inbound link removal never mirrors, and outbound CREATE never binds to existing issues) must be measured as platform constraints rather than bridge defects, with cells correctly reporting them as expected red and defects filed as epic children.
